fact: FAO SWALIM states its remote sensing unit has used medium- and high-resolution satellite images to estimate cultivable areas and estimated production by cropping system at regional and district level.
system: SWALIM remote sensing and image analysis unit

fact: FSNAU published E-MODIS NDVI maps of Somalia showing vegetation deviations from short-term averages, month by month from January 2007 to July 2026.

HoA DRIVE reports that satellite monitoring of vegetation triggered drought Takaful payouts in Hiiraan, Galguduud, Lower Shabelle, Bay and Middle Shabelle under the World Bank-financed Index-Based Livestock Takaful programme, supported by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Livestock, Forestry and Range, with ACRE Africa calculating payouts from satellite data.

HoA DRIVE reports 17,373 pastoralists received US$3.43 million in September 2026 payouts triggered by satellite vegetation monitoring, after an earlier round in March 2026 reaching about 17,734 pastoralists.

FAO says the SWALIM programme's geospatial unit identifies suitable growing conditions for at least 14 crops to guide investment and land-use planning, using very-high-resolution satellite image analysis among its capabilities.
